sources.role: Sole canonical paper-only evaluation implementation; no copied risk domain
Exact externally pinned native contract authority
Source identity and independent expected bundle pin conventions; no replacement implementation
Callable bytes-to-bytes transport, 4194304-byte input and 2000000-byte response boundary

abi.storage: Caller-owned disjoint buffers; no retained pointers, allocator handles, returned C strings or callbacks

sourceIdentityAlgorithm.name: vertex-kernel-source-v1
sourceIdentityAlgorithm.algorithm: SHA256 of UTF-8 vertex-kernel-source-v1 followed by NUL, then each sorted services-relative slash-separated path followed by NUL and raw 32-byte SHA256 of file bytes. Symlink source entries rejected. Build compares actual digest to independently reviewed VERTEX_KERNEL_SOURCE_SHA256.
sourceIdentityAlgorithm.contractIdentity: The independently reviewed sourceDigest inside the actual externally pinned authority bundle; embedded at build and checked during native bundle loading.

ffiSourceReview: Pointer ranges checked for integer overflow, isize length, null/nonempty, length-cell alignment and all-region overlap before constructing slices.
Foreign caller remains responsible for real allocation validity, immutability and lifetime; arithmetic cannot prove pointers safe.
Rust result Vec drops before return; output copy uses caller capacity and written count; insufficient capacity writes no output bytes.
Unwind panics mapped to fixed status; abort/OOM/invalid pointers are not recoverable. No global panic hook mutation.
Only the existing ContractAuthority and exact existing kernel evaluate_json decide domain output; rejection JSON remains a successful ABI response.
Input/output/bundle limits are safety ceilings, not latency or maximum RSS proofs; authority is reconstructed per call.
loaderSourceReview: No import-time file reads, library selection, environment discovery or native load.
Explicit reviewed absolute image path copied into bounded memfd, full externally pinned SHA256 checked before dlopen, write/grow/shrink/seal seals enforced.
Exact canonical build identity bytes checked, not permissive JSON field coercion.
Pinned bundle is natively validated before a bridge instance is returned; absent configuration has no fallback.
At most eight process-lifetime native mappings/descriptors, including mapped images that fail ABI inspection; close retires bundle bytes without unsafe dlclose.
One call per bridge, fail-fast busy; async offloads locally and shields native work from waiter cancellation; no timeout claim or retry.
unverifiedLimitations: No build, import, execution, test, typecheck, formatter, linter, probe, installation, network, DB access or generation performed for this source handoff.
No artifact digest, build ID, contract bundle digest or reviewed dependency lock has been created or fabricated.
Linux memfd, procfs, ELF loader and Python 3.12.11 only; platform behavior remains untested.

A reviewed ELF image is trusted executable code. External release verification must seal its native dependency closure, loader environment, toolchain and runtime permissions. A primary-image hash is not a sandbox.
In-process OOM, abort, process faults and native deadline enforcement require host supervision; Python cannot forcibly cancel a native call.

Rust parity regression requires VERTEX_KERNEL_TEST_BUNDLE and independent VERTEX_KERNEL_TEST_BUNDLE_SHA256 matching compiled contract source identity; it must not be skipped or replaced with permissive generated schemas.
Successful admission parity with fully qualified market/calendar/Greek/policy/journal fixtures remains a final integration acceptance responsibility.
